pr_body:
When `_stop` gets called with `stop_at_checkpoint=true` and at the same time a transform got triggered internally or externally a race condition could lead to a deadlock of `5s`. The change fixes the situation where 2 lock objects could lock one another.

fixes #75846
pr_title: [Transform] fix potential deadlock when using stop_at_checkpoint
pr_comment:
> It might be good to bump test logging up to debug?

It is already on debug. 

> I am wondering if this will really fix the issue.

It does not fix the issue (this PR _relates_ only to the issue)

> 
> The listener would have gotten an error when trying to wait for stop at checkpoint on a timeout. So, I am not sure increasing the timeout here fixes it. Did the logs in the issue show that the stop call failed?

yes:
```
[2021-08-02T05:07:00,126][ERROR][o.e.x.t.t.TransformIndexer] [javaRestTest-2] [transform-wait-for-checkpoint] Timed out (5s) waiting for transform state to be stored.
```

Of course, this could also be a race condition where the listener is not called. If the problem appears again with the `10s` timeout it is unlikely a timeout again, but a race.

> 
> It seems like race condition where the task is removed from cluster state before its previous state is fully

This PR does _not_ fix #75846, I am still investigating. I see a new task created before the old one has been completely removed. But this happens after the timeout or race condition above.

I hope to get more info when it happens again, the `cause` in stop was missing. Next time we should get the full stack trace.

as for the race, I think here is one:

```
[2021-08-02T05:06:55,168][DEBUG][o.e.x.t.t.ClientTransformIndexer] [javaRestTest-2] [transform-wait-for-checkpoint] Updated state document from [{seqNo=9,primaryTerm=1,index=.transform-internal-007}] to [{seqNo=10,primaryTerm=1,index=.transform-internal-007}]
[2021-08-02T05:07:00,126][ERROR][o.e.x.t.t.TransformIndexer] [javaRestTest-2] [transform-wait-for-checkpoint] Timed out (5s) waiting for transform state to be stored.
```

It's suspicious that the time between the 2 log lines is roughly `5s`. I see a `synchronized` method and a countdown latch, this sounds like a deadly mixture. But I still don't see the issue, will add more debug logging.
@hendrikmuhs I am wondering if we will see that delay be `10s` after this PR :D. I think there is a thread dead-lock there. The fact that its SOO close to 5 seconds is very suspicious.

Found it:

| Thread 1 (transport of stop)                   | Thread 2 (task/scheduler)                        |
|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| **(s)** task->stop_at_checkpoint               |                                                  |
|                                                | **(s)** task->triggered() (**lock A**)           |
| **(s)** indexer->save_state (**lock B**)       |                                                  |
|                                                | **(s)** indexer->triggered (**wait for lock B**) |
| **(s)** task->shutdown() (**wait for lock A**) |                                                  |
|                                                |                                                  |
| _timeout_ (**unlock B**)                       |                                                  |
|                                                | **(s)** indexer->triggered (**lock B**)          |


The problem are 2 locks of the task and the indexer that can lock one another. 

Interesting is the `task->stop_at_checkpoint` which is `synchronized` but as it moves the execution of
the thread:

```
        // move the call to the generic thread pool, so we do not block the network thread
        getThreadPool().executor(ThreadPool.Names.GENERIC)
            .execute(() -> { getIndexer().setStopAtCheckpoint(shouldStopAtCheckpoint, shouldStopAtCheckpointListener); });
```

it unlocks the _task_ (lock A) and therefore allows the trigger originating from the scheduler to acquire lock A.

I incorporated the new findings ans inspected all code paths where the indexer thread gets locked 1st and 2nd the task. With that change:

 - all calls either lock the task or the indexer
 - if it's required to lock both, it locks the task 1st and the indexer 2nd
 	- it might call task->indexer->task, however as locks are re-entrant, that's not a problem

review_comment: to fix the deadlock we don't initiate the shutdown in this place.

the thread switch is the only change, otherwise the code below is unchanged.

By moving the thread switch, the `transformTask.setShouldStopAtCheckpoint` call does not unlock the class lock of the task.
instead of calling `doSaveState` we call persist, which simplifies a lot, because `doSaveState` makes a lot of other checks that aren't necessary for this case.
this method has been moved from ClientTransformIndexer without changes
this is the origin of the deadlock, by moving to another thread we unlocked the task (this method is `synchronized`).
the shutdown now happens in the thread that locked the task and the indexer. shutdown locks the task once more.
